test-eng-01.archetype: Strong fit: 4-8 years at a NewSpace or small-satellite company doing almost exactly this job, lives near the role location, right to work.

test-eng-09.archetype: Returner after a 2-3 year career break with strong relevant experience before it.

test-eng-10.archetype: Academic: PhD or postdoc whose research is relevant to the role, little industry delivery experience.

test-eng-12.archetype: Contractor with many 6-12 month stints, relevant tools, unclear depth or ownership.

test-eng-13.archetype: Fresh international MSc graduate in aerospace with a generic CV, no projects matching the role, needs sponsorship.

test-eng-14.archetype: Adjacent discipline mismatch: an engineer from a neighbouring but wrong discipline (for example web developer for embedded, mechanical for electronics) who believes skills will transfer.

test-eng-15.archetype: Generic AI-written application: buzzwords, vague claims, no concrete projects, numbers or tools.

test-eng-16.archetype: Mass applicant: the cover letter names a different company or a different job title by mistake.

test-eng-17.archetype: Technician-level applicant (HNC/apprenticeship, hands-on lab or production work) applying for an engineer role that needs more design depth.

test-eng-18.archetype: Unrelated background (sales, finance, retail, hospitality) who is passionate about space and did an online course.

test-eng-19.archetype: Decent experience but in an unrelated engineering domain (for example HVAC, civil, process engineering) with little overlap.

test-eng-20.archetype: Strong on paper but the application is sloppy: typos, inconsistent dates, a CV that contradicts the cover letter.
